newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland hails EU move as "approval from auditors".
newsitem.headline: Poland hails EU move as "approval from auditors".

text.p: Warsaw welcomed on Tuesday a European Union decision to include Poland among countries due to start entry talks as an acknowledgement of the effort Poles have made towards membership.
"We feel like an enterprise that has received the approval of its auditors," said Jaroslaw Pietras, deputy minister in Poland's committee overseeing the EU membership drive.

A meeting of the EU executive commission on Tuesday adopted its Agenda 2000 document, agreeing to include Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia as well as Cyprus in the union's most ambitious expansion to date.
The document will be formally presented to the European Parliament on Wednesday.

"We are pleased with the document itself. We see it as very useful in the whole process of accepting Poland into the EU, because it is an expression of an external, objective opinion," Pietras told Reuters.

Although Poland, which escaped Soviet military and economic domination only in 1989, is strongly determined to bind itself to Western structures, its relations with the economic organisation have been troubled by a series of trade disputes.
Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski's spokesman Antoni Styrczula said that if the decision were confirmed on Wednesday, it would mean Poland could start entry talks in January next year.
It would also confirm Poland on the road to the second of its two key foreign policy priorities, after this month's Madrid summit of NATO invited the country to start entry talks, he told Reuters.

"The decision would mean an expression of the good state of Poland's preparations for entering the EU and would be an element of consolidation of the political and trade relations between our country and the EU," he said.

EU officials have repeatedly reproached Warsaw over issues ranging from the way in which Korea's Daewoo car producer assembles cars in Poland, through protection of its oil and steel industries, down to duties on Scotch whisky.

They have also urged the country to hasten the laborious process of adjusting its laws and procedures to EU standards and expressed doubts about the state of Polish agriculture, with its many small and inefficiant farms.
In early June Pietras said in Brussels that Polish public opinion should brace itself for criticism when the EU published its opinion on its readiness.

The Polish Rzeczpospolita daily reported from Brussels earlier on Tuesday that the European Commission document would say that Poland had a chance of getting into the EU in 2002 or 2003 -- if it reformed its economy enough by then to stand a competitive chance in the single market.
